plan.title: Creating a Restricted List Rule
plan.summary: From People oversight > Trade monitoring, open Flagging rules, choose the Restricted securities template, and walk through the rule wizard (name, criteria, securities, who it covers, review) to publish a restricted list rule.
steps: Navigate to People oversight > Trade monitoring
Click the "Flagging rules" button in the page header of "Trade monitoring" to open the rules list.
Click "Create rule" in the header of the "Flagging rules" page to open the "Create a rule" gallery.
On the "Restricted securities" card, click "Use this template" to open the "Restricted securities" wizard.
On the "Name & overview" step, type a name into the "Rule name" field (for example "Deal team restricted list"), optionally fill "Description", leave "Run indefinitely" on, then click "Next".
On the "Restriction criteria" step, keep the "Symbols" card selected under "What the rule restricts", keep "Flag matching trades" selected under "Behavior", then click "Next".

On the "Securities" step, type tickers into the "Search by ticker, name or CUSIP, or paste a list" box, click "Add" (or use "Upload CSV" for a file), confirm the rows appear in the table (columns Identifier, Type, Start, End), then click "Next".
On the "Who it covers" step, leave the "Apply to everyone" switch on (or turn it off and pick employee groups or individuals in "Search for employee groups or individuals..."), then click "Next".
On the "Review & publish" step, check the "In the rule list" summary and leave the "Active" switch on, then click "Publish" in the page header and wait for the "Rule published" toast.
prerequisites: Hadrius Academy must have the People oversight employee-compliance module on (company feature "employee_c8e"); otherwise the sidebar shows "Code of ethics" and no "Trade monitoring" child (use_employee_tab.tsx).

The user needs trade-monitoring read access (useHasTradeMonitoringReadAccessOptimistic) to see the "Trade monitoring" tab, and the "employee_compliance.trade_monitoring.edit_restrictions" permission, because the "Flagging rules" button only renders when hasEditRestrictions is true (tab_trade_monitor_dashboard.tsx).

The company needs the new rule builder flag (employee_compliance_config.new_rule_builder_enabled) for the "Create rule" button, the gallery and the wizard. useRuleBuilderGuard redirects to /employees/trade-monitoring/settings without it. I could not read Hadrius Academy's flag value because the company lookup tool was denied.

If that flag is off, the same page shows an "Add" button instead, which opens the older single-page form at /employees/trade-monitoring/add. There you pick "Security list" in "Rule type", enter a "Rule name", upload a CSV/XLSX, and click "Accept valid rows". The steps above do not apply to that form.
Optional: employee groups or individuals must exist if the rule should cover specific people rather than "Apply to everyone".

plan.title: How to Compare Versions
plan.summary: Open a marketing document that has at least two parsed versions, choose "Compare versions" from the version dropdown, pick an earlier version to compare against, and review the changes side by side.
steps: Navigate to Marketing > Projects
Click the horizontal-ellipsis (three-dot) button at the top right of the project card that contains the document, then click "View project" in the "Actions" popover.
On the "Project details page", find the document in the "Workflow & document progress" table and click "View" in its Actions column.
In the document review header, click the version dropdown button (labelled "Version V<n>", for example V3).
Click "Compare versions" in the dropdown menu to open the comparison page.
Click "Pick a version" in the left panel, then choose an earlier version (for example "V1") under "Compare against".
Wait for the sidebar to finish generating and list the changes, then click "Tables" in the "Change content type" switcher to show the table changes (use "Text" or "Images" for the other types).
Click "Back to review" at the top left to return to the document.
prerequisites: The Marketing module must be enabled for the Hadrius Academy company and the user must have Marketing access (MarketingProjectsPage checks useCompanyHasFeature("marketing_review") and useCanAccessMarketing()).

The company's Marketing review config must have enable_version_comparison set to true. Otherwise the "Compare versions" menu item is hidden and the compare page shows "Comparison unavailable" (component_compare_versions_menu_item.tsx, use_version_comparison_feature.ts). I could not check this value for Hadrius Academy because the company lookup was not permitted.

A marketing project with a document that has at least 2 versions parsed by Reducto. Otherwise the menu item is disabled with the text "Version comparison requires at least 2 versions parsed beginning in March 2026." (reducto_version_helpers.ts canCompareDocumentVersions). Older versions parsed before March 2026 may not qualify.
The document must be reviewable (not "Processing" or in an error state) so that the "View" button appears (component_project_docs_workflow_progress.tsx isDocumentReady).

plan.title: Platform Tour: Home, Sidebar, and Navigation
plan.summary: Tour the Home dashboard, then the sidebar's header, parent tabs and sub-tabs, and its collapse control, ending on the People directory page.
steps: Navigate to Platform > Home (/home)
Point out the "Home" page header, the "N items need your attention" description under it, and the "Refresh" button at its right; click "Refresh".
Scroll the Home page's grid of module cards (for example "Testing program", "Certifications", "Disclosures", "Email"), each showing a count and either "Needs attention" or "No action needed".
In the sidebar header, point to the company picker button showing the current company name (Hadrius Academy), then click the Hadrius logo link (aria-label "Home") to show it returns to Home.
In the sidebar, click the parent tab "Testing program" to expand it and show its sub-tabs "Tests" and "Findings" ("Policies", "Calendar" and the others appear when the user is an admin).
Click the parent tab "People oversight" to expand it and show its sub-tabs, such as "Certifications" and "Accounts".

If the user is an admin with access to more than one company, the sidebar also shows an "Overview" tab (shouldUseOverviewHome) and the logo link goes to /home, which is still a valid route.

plan.title: Setting Up Your Account: Email, Password, and MFA
plan.summary: On the Account tab of Settings, change your sign-in email (with a confirmation code), change your password, and turn on authenticator-app MFA.
steps: Navigate to Settings > Account (/settings/account)
In the "Update email address" card, type the new address into "New email address".
Type the same address into "Confirm new email address".
Click "Update email address" and wait for the "Confirmation code" field to appear in the same card.
In the "Change password" card, type your existing password into "Current password".
Type the new password into "New password".
Type the new password again into "Confirm new password".
Click "Change password" and wait for the message "Your password has been updated."

In the "Multi-factor authentication (MFA)" card, scan the QR code (or copy the code with the "Copy MFA setup code" icon button) into your authenticator app, then type the 6-digit code into "Verify TOTP code".
Click "Verify code" and wait for the "Success" dialog ("Your multi-factor authentication (MFA) setting has been successfully updated."), then click "OK".
prerequisites: The signed-in user must have password login enabled (user.can_use_password_login). Without it the "Change password" card is not rendered (page_account_settings.tsx:642). SSO-only users will not see it.
A real inbox for the new email address. The "Confirmation code" is emailed, and confirming it signs the user out (component_edit_email_address.tsx: submitConfirmationCode calls signOut()).
An authenticator app (TOTP) for the MFA step. If MFA is already "Enabled", the card only offers disabling it, with no QR code.
No admin role or feature flag is required. The Account tab is not gated in component_account_settings_header.tsx.

plan.title: Switching Between Admin and Employee View
plan.summary: An admin who also has an active employee record uses the "Use as employee" button in the Settings header to switch the app into the employee experience, checks the employee dashboard, then uses "Use as admin" on Settings to switch back.
steps: Navigate to Settings > Account (the "Account" tab on the "Settings" page, at /settings/account).
Confirm the Settings page header, titled "Settings", shows the "Use as employee" button (user icon) at the top right, next to the red "Sign out" button.
Click the "Use as employee" button.

Wait for the left sidebar to change from the admin navigation, which includes "People directory", to the employee navigation, which starts with "Dashboard" and "Profile" and ends with "Settings". "People directory" should no longer appear.
Click "Dashboard" in the employee sidebar (/employee/dashboard).
Wait for the "Hello <first name>!" heading and the line "Review your compliance status and any required actions below."
Click "Settings" in the employee sidebar (/account, which redirects to /settings/account).
Click the "Use as admin" button in the Settings page header. The same button now shows this label instead of "Use as employee".
Wait for the admin sidebar to reappear, with the "People directory" tab visible again.
prerequisites: The signed-in user is an admin (user.is_admin) with admin view in the selected company.
That user has a linked employee record in the selected company (user.linked_employees contains the company).
The company's People oversight feature (employee_c8e) is ACTIVE. Without it the switch button is not rendered.
The linked employee's onboarding_status is not PENDING. Otherwise the dashboard shows the onboarding home instead of the "Hello <first name>!" heading.

plan.title: Completing Your Firm Setup Checklist
plan.summary: An administrator opens the full-screen "Get ready to go live" checklist from the sidebar, jumps between modules, filters out finished items, launches an item's call-to-action, then comes back with "Return to setup".
steps: Navigate to Platform > Complete setup (the "Complete setup" button at the bottom of the left sidebar, route /admin-onboarding)
Wait for the full-screen page headed "Get ready to go live" (overline "Administrator setup") to finish loading.
In the "Your progress" card on the left, read the "N of M complete" line and the progress bar below it.
In the "Onboarding modules" navigation on the left, click a module name (for example "People Directory") to scroll to that section.
In the module section, read the "N of M" counter at the top right of the section header, and the group headings inside it (for example "Onboarding" and "Customization").
Turn on the "Hide completed" switch under the module list to hide finished items, then turn it off again.

In an item that shows "Not complete", click its outline call-to-action button (for example "Manage groups" under "Create custom groups and permissions"). This opens the page where the task is done (/employees/settings?tab=groups).
Wait for the banner reading "Continue working through your setup checklist." to appear at the top of the page that opened.
Click "Return to setup" in that banner to go back to /admin-onboarding.
Check the item's status and the counters. Completed items show "Complete" with a check mark and a struck-through title, and the "N of M" counters and the progress bar update.
Click "Skip for now" (link-style button in the top-right of the header) to leave the checklist and go to the app home.
prerequisites: Signed in as a user with the ADMIN role. Other roles are redirected to /employee/dashboard (page_admin_onboarding.tsx).
The sidebar "Complete setup" button only shows when the checklist API returns show_in_nav true. Otherwise open /admin-onboarding directly.
The modules and items shown come from the company's checklist data (seeded in the backend and based on the products in the plan), so the exact modules vary by company.

platform::addingemployeessingleaddvscsvi.title: Adding Employees: Single Add vs. CSV Import

plan.title: Adding Employees: Single Add vs. CSV Import
plan.summary: Add one employee with the Manual form on the Add employees page, then add several at once with Bulk upload by importing a CSV and confirming the review table.
steps: Navigate to People oversight > People directory
Click "Add employees" in the table toolbar next to "Export" to open the "Add employees" page, which starts on the "Manual" tab.
Type the employee's first name into the "First name" field under "Employee details".
Type the employee's last name into the "Last name" field.

Type a valid address into the "Email address" field (leave "Middle name" and the optional "Employment start date" empty; "Assign to group(s)" and "Assign permission(s)" default to "Employees" and "Employee").
Click "Add employee" at the top right and wait for the "Employee added" toast; the app returns to the People directory.
Click "Add employees" again to reopen the "Add employees" page.
Click "Bulk upload" in the Manual / Bulk upload switcher to show the "Upload employees via CSV" section (the "Download CSV template" button sits in that section's header).
Upload a .csv file in the dropzone ("Upload a .csv file with employee data") and wait for the "Review imported employees" table, which shows "N valid" badges once every row passes.
Click "Confirm import" at the top right and wait for the "Employees added" toast; the app returns to the People directory.
prerequisites: The signed-in user can open the People directory. The page is ungated by module (page_people_oversight_upsell.tsx: "The people directory is part of Hadrius base; never module-gated"). Whether a specific role may submit the add is enforced by the backend and I did not check it.
Single add: use an email address not already in the company.
CSV import: have a .csv file ready (the template comes from "Download CSV template") with first name, last name and email per row, and no duplicate emails in the file.
If the CSV names groups or permissions, they must match existing ones exactly, since names are case-sensitive; unmatched names show as "Unrecognized" warnings in the review table.

steps.quote: description="Upload a .csv file with employee data"

The People directory itself is not module-gated (use_tabs.tsx and page_people_oversight_upsell.tsx both say it is part of Hadrius base).

plan.title: Managing the Document Libarary
plan.summary: Create a folder in the Document library, upload files, open a file to see its versions, rename it, and archive it, in the Hadrius Academy company.
steps: Navigate to Documents > Document library (sidebar item "Documents", route /document_library)

Type the folder name into the "Name" field, then click "Create" and wait for the toast "Folder created".

plan.title: Roles vs. Groups: Assigning Roles and Module-Level Access
plan.summary: Create a custom permissions profile (the role) in People directory settings, switch on module-level access such as Marketing review, then open its members to assign people, which is how a role differs from a plain group tag.
steps: Navigate to People oversight > People directory
Click the "Permissions & groups" button in the page header to open the employee settings page, which lands on the "Groups" tab.
Click the "Permissions" tab in the "Employee settings sections" tab bar.
Click "New permissions profile" in the page header to open the "Create new permissions profile" dialog.
Type a name (for example "Marketing Reviewers") into the "Permissions profile name" field.
Click "Create permissions profile"; the new profile is selected in the "All permissions profiles" sidebar under "Custom".

Scroll to the "Marketing review" section and turn on the "Submit marketing materials for review" switch.
Click "Save" to store the module-level access.
Click "Manage members" to open the profile's linked group on the "Groups" tab, where "Add members" assigns people to the role.

The "Marketing review" section always renders in the Permissions tab; the module itself may still be inactive for the company.

plan.title: Using the Template Library (certification, disclosure, branch exam, firm oversight)
plan.summary: Open the Template library (Platform), filter the table by template type, create a new Certification template from scratch, confirm it as a draft, and find it under the Drafts filter.
steps: Navigate to Platform > Template library (sidebar item "Templates", or Settings > Product > Platform > "Template library"); the page header reads "Template library".

Click the type filter dropdown (placeholder "All template types") in the toolbar above the table and choose "Certification" from its options; the options are "Branch exam", "Certification", "Disclosure", "Disclosure review" and "Firm oversight", limited to the types enabled for the firm. The "Type" column then shows only Certification templates.
Click the "Create template" button (plus icon) at the right of the search row, next to the "Search by template name" field, to open the "Create a new template" dialog.
If the dialog shows two tabs, click "Start from scratch" (the other tab is "Generate with AI").
Click the "Template name" field (placeholder "e.g. 2026 tri-annual branch exam") and type a name for the template.
Click the dropdown showing "Select a module" under "Module" and choose "Certification".

Click "Create template" (with an arrow icon) in the dialog footer; it is disabled until a name and module are set. The template builder opens with a "Save as draft" button and a "Preview" button in the header.
Click "Save as draft" in the builder header.
In the "Save template as draft?" dialog, click "Save draft", then wait for the toast "Template saved as draft". The app then returns to the Template library.
Click "Drafts" in the status filter row above the table to show the new Certification template with its Draft status badge.
prerequisites: The user must be allowed to read templates. If the templates request is permission-denied, the page shows a "Template Library" access-restricted view and the sidebar item is hidden (templates_dashboard.tsx, use_tabs.tsx).

The "Create template" button only appears if the user can manage at least one template type. For Certification that is the permission template_library.employee_templates.certifications.manage (templates_dashboard.tsx, useAvailableModuleSections).

A type appears in the filter and in the "Module" dropdown only if the firm's template-config includes it. "Firm oversight" only appears if that module is enabled for the firm, and it needs the permission template_library.firm_oversight_templates.manage to create.
The "Start from scratch" / "Generate with AI" tabs only appear for users with template_library.all.admin. Other users see the scratch form directly.

platform::connectinganintegrationandtest.title: Connecting an Integration and Testing the Connection

plan.title: Connecting an Integration and Testing the Connection
plan.summary: In Settings, open the Integrations tab, choose an integration, enter its connection details and click Connect, then run Test connection to verify the saved credentials.
steps: Navigate to Settings > Integrations (route /settings/integrations). From any page, click the icon-only gear link with aria-label "Settings" at the right of the sidebar header, then click the "Integrations" tab.
Click the "Search integrations" box and type the integration's name to filter the list. The "Grid" and "List" switcher is also available.

On the card or row for the integration, click the outline button "Connect". It reads "Manage" if the integration is already connected and "Learn more" if your firm is not eligible. The detail page opens with the URL /settings/integrations?integration=<slug>.
Read the "Setup guide" section, which is expanded while the integration is not connected, to see which values you need to gather.

In the "Connection details" section, fill in every field listed. Labels are generated from the backend field names (for example "API key" or "Client ID") and depend on the integration. Password fields show the placeholder "••••••••". Date fields show "Select a date", and dropdown fields show "Select an option".

Click the button at the bottom right of "Connection details". It reads "Connect" for a new connection and "Save changes" for an existing one, and it stays disabled until at least one field has been changed.

Wait for the green alert titled "Success" under the fields (a red "Something went wrong" alert means the save failed). The "Status" badge in the "At a glance" sidebar changes to "Connected" and a "Test connection" section appears.
In the "Test connection" section, click the outline button "Test connection" at the top right of the section. Its description reads "Verify the saved connection using the stored credentials."
Wait for the alert titled "Connection works". If the credentials are wrong, the alert is titled "Connection failed" instead.
prerequisites: You must be an admin or superadmin, or hold the "platform.integrations.configure" permission. Otherwise /settings/integrations redirects to /settings/account and the "Integrations" tab is hidden.

The integration must not be marked disabled for the firm. If disabled, its card shows a "Not available" badge, the button reads "Learn more", and the detail page has no form or "Test connection" section.
You need valid credentials for the chosen integration from the vendor. The "Test connection" section only appears once the integration is connected.
The integration must expose form fields. An OAuth-style connector with no fields shows no "Connection details" section.

plan.title: Customizing Email Branding (logo, greeting, footer)
plan.summary: In Settings > Email notifications > Branding, open the Edit design panel and set the email logo, greeting and footer content, with autosave and a live preview.
steps: Navigate to Settings > Email notifications > Branding (/settings/email-notifications/branding)
Click the "Edit design" button above the email preview to open the design panel; the header shows the "Edit design" title.
On the "Header" segment, under the "Custom logo" section, drop or select a PNG (up to 2MB) in the file dropzone; wait for the "Logo uploaded" toast.
Click the "Content" segment in the design panel.
In the "Greeting" section, type your greeting (for example "Hi there,") into the "Greeting" field; the preview updates and a "Saved your ..." toast appears after autosave.
Click the "Footer" segment in the design panel.
In the "Footer content" section, type into the "Support email" field.
In the "Footer content" section, type into the "Tagline" field and wait for the success toast.
Click the "Content" segment, then in the "Fine print" section click "Add footer copy" and type into the rich-text box (placeholder "A disclaimer, a mailing address…").
Click the icon-only "Close design panel" button (X at the right of the panel header) to view the final branded email in the preview.
prerequisites: Company must have the "email_log" feature enabled (useCompanyHasFeature("email_log") in page_notification_hub.tsx); Hadrius Academy needs it on.

User needs the platform.notification_hub.read permission to see the page, and platform.notification_hub.resolve ("Email notifications" resolve permission) to edit; otherwise the tab shows a "Read only" alert and fields are disabled.
A PNG logo file up to 2MB to upload (file upload handled by the recorder).
The footer color section only appears once a company logo is uploaded; no other data is required.

plan.title: Getting Started with Ask Hadrius
plan.summary: From the Home page, open the Ask Hadrius panel from the sidebar, send a question about your workspace, then start a new chat and revisit past conversations from the panel header.
steps: Navigate to Platform > Home (click "Home" at the top of the sidebar navigation, route /home)
Click the "Ask Hadrius" button (sparkle icon) in the sidebar header, below the company picker, to open the Ask Hadrius panel.
Wait for the panel to show the header title "Ask Hadrius" and the heading "Ask about your workspace", with the label "Suggested for this page" above a few suggested question cards.
Click into the text box with the placeholder "Ask Hadrius..." (accessible name "Ask Hadrius prompt") at the bottom of the panel.
Type a question into the "Ask Hadrius prompt" text box, for example "Which modules need attention?".
Click the round arrow-up icon button labelled "Send message" at the right end of the text box.

Wait for the reply to start streaming: the send button turns into the square-icon "Stop response" button, the sidebar button's label becomes "Ask Hadrius, working", and a thinking indicator appears at the bottom of the chat.
Click the icon-only pencil-square button labelled "New chat" (tooltip "New chat"), the second icon at the left of the panel header, to start a fresh conversation.

Click the icon-only three-line menu button labelled "Conversations" (tooltip "Conversations"), the first icon at the left of the panel header, and wait for the header title to change to "Conversations" and the "Search conversations" field to appear.
Click the "Back" button (left-arrow icon) at the left of the panel header to return to the chat.
prerequisites: The company must have the ASK_HADRIUS feature flag (useCompanyHasFeatureFlag("ASK_HADRIUS") in useCanAccessAskHadrius); without it the sidebar button and panel are not rendered.
The user's role must have the "Ask Hadrius read access" permission (ask_hadrius.all.read_access), set under role permissions; without it the sidebar button is hidden.
The "Conversations" list only shows entries after at least one chat exists; otherwise it shows "No conversations yet". Step 6 creates the first one.
